cards.explanation: The answer is False, friends. When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid and trembled violently (1 Samuel 28:5). A king with a whole army gathered behind him, and his body is still doing its own thing. Afraid and shaking, that's the picture the text gives.

The answer is that He does not answer Saul, friends. Saul inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him by dreams or Urim or prophets (1 Samuel 28:6). Three ways Saul might have heard from Him, and none of them brought a word. I think that's a heavy moment, and Saul feels it.

The word is medium, friends. Saul tells his servants, “Find me a woman who is a medium, so I can go and consult her.” His servants answer that there is a medium at Endor (1 Samuel 28:7). Saul had removed the mediums from the land (1 Samuel 28:3), so this request stands out.

The answer is that he puts on different clothes, friends. Saul disguises himself by putting on different clothes, and he sets out with two of his men (1 Samuel 28:8). The text doesn't say why he does it, but I think a king in a costume is the kind of thing nobody forgets. I've worn my apron and chef's hat so long I'd never pull off a disguise.

The answer is that she asks why he set a trap to get her killed, friends. She says, “Surely you know what Saul has done, how he has killed the mediums and spiritists in the land. Why have you set a trap to get me killed?” (1 Samuel 28:9). Think about that. The disguise works so well that she's complaining about Saul to Saul.

The answer is True, friends. Saul swears to her by the LORD: “As surely as the LORD lives, no punishment shall come upon you for this.” (1 Samuel 28:10). She had just asked why he was setting a trap to get her killed, so he answers her fear with a promise.

The name is Samuel, friends. The woman asks whom she should bring up, and Saul says, “Bring up Samuel…” (1 Samuel 28:11). Samuel, a prophet of the LORD (1 Samuel 3:20), had already died and been buried in Ramah (1 Samuel 28:3). He's the one Saul asks for by name.

The answer is False, friends. When she sees Samuel, she cries out in a loud voice. Then she says to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!” (1 Samuel 28:12). Calm and quiet was not on the menu.
She describes an old man wearing a robe, friends. She says, “An old man is coming up…” and then, “And he is wearing a robe.” (1 Samuel 28:14). Right after that, the text says Saul knew it was Samuel.
The answer is True, friends. Once Saul knew it was Samuel, he bowed facedown in reverence (1 Samuel 28:14). This is the king who walked in wearing a disguise. Now he's flat on his face.

The answer is that Saul wants Samuel to tell him what to do, friends. Saul says the Philistines are fighting against him and God no longer answers him. Then he says, “So I have called on you to tell me what to do.” (1 Samuel 28:15). He wants a plan from Samuel.

The name is David, friends. Samuel says the LORD has torn the kingdom out of Saul's hand and given it to his neighbor David (1 Samuel 28:17). Samuel adds that the LORD has done exactly what He spoke through him. David is the name Samuel gives.

The answer is False, friends. Samuel says the LORD did this because Saul did not obey Him or carry out His burning anger against Amalek (1 Samuel 28:18). Fighting the Philistines isn't the reason Samuel gives. The reason he names is about obeying the LORD.

The answer is True, friends. Samuel says the LORD will deliver Israel with Saul into the hand of the Philistines. He says it again about the army of Israel (1 Samuel 28:19). It's a hard thing to hear, and I think it hits Saul hard.

Saul falls flat on the ground, friends. Immediately he falls, terrified by the words of Samuel (1 Samuel 28:20). The text also says his strength was gone because he hadn't eaten anything all that day and night. That's one tired, scared king.

She wants to set some bread before him, friends. She asks to set a morsel of bread before him so he may eat and have the strength to go on his way (1 Samuel 28:22). Saul hadn't eaten anything all that day and night. Someone offering bread gets my attention every time.
The answer is False, friends. Saul refuses, saying, “I will not eat.” He doesn't give in until his servants join the woman in urging him. Then he heeds their voice (1 Samuel 28:23).
The word is servants, friends. Saul's servants join the woman in urging him to eat (1 Samuel 28:23). Saul had first said, “I will not eat.” After they urged him, the text says he heeded their voice.

The word is night, friends. The text says that night they got up and left (1 Samuel 28:25). They came to the woman at night (1 Samuel 28:8), so the whole visit happens in the dark. Full of bread, off they go.
